parsed.why: Border pride-welcome programme, marriage equality, mature trans healthcare, society ahead of law. Costs: no hate-crime recourse, one tourist-perpetrated killing, uncertain detention placement and a documented ward refusal — real but scattered, not state-directed.

State-directed targeting: mass arrests through 2026 including at a border post, penalties doubled, new ban explicitly naming transsexuality, UPR rejections of protections, mob body-burning with impunity. No recourse; active enforcement dominates.

Patterned lethal shootings of trans women (2024-2026 'wave'), religious court branding trans women rapists-in-disguise, care denial contributing to a death, sodomy law, failed implementation despite protective statute. State bystander, thin recourse.

Sodomy criminalised but enforcement undocumented; dated 2015 killings; official hostility and closed civic space offset by police-escorted Pride, broadcasting hate-speech rules and inclusive health policy. Mixed signals, no trans-specific targeting recorded.

Law-enforcement stigma with documented police blackmail, frequent attacks surging after state anti-LGBT reforms, hostile legislative-media trajectory, care barred under 25, recognition revoked. Same-sex conduct legal, but police as perpetrators removes recourse.
